summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported that Tom Allen, found at the Champion's Rest on Washington Avenue, dismissed reports that Jem Mace had accepted his challenge as a New York scheme and repeated that he had retired from the ring.

metadata.notes: masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Monday Morning, July 19, 1875

facts.fact: Allen's saloon on Washington Avenue was called the "Champion's Rest"
places: Champion's Rest, Washington Avenue, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen denied reports that he had challenged Jem Mace and that Mace had accepted, saying he would never again enter the ring
Ned O'Baldwin wanted Allen to tour the country with him giving sparring exhibitions; Allen declined

notes: Early use of the name Champion's Rest for the Washington Avenue saloon (likely 417, see facts 009/017). Paper says Allen is well fixed financially and has a family to care for.
